newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cen.bank says plans no further gold sales.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cen.bank says plans no further gold sales.

text.p: The Belgian central bank, which has been a major seller of gold in recent years, said it planned no further sales.

"When I became governor (in 1990) we had 1,300 tonnes of gold. Now we have 600 tonnes. We did enough. I can live with our current level of gold assets," central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse told a news conference on Wednesday on the bank's annual report. His comments were embargoed for Friday.
"Given the current gold price on the market...I think many other countries are unhappy that they have not done what we did," he added.
Belgium's most recent gold sale was in March when the bank sold 203 tonnes to an unspecified central bank. Gold was then quoted at around $400 an ounce. It was at $345 on Wednesday.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
